checks: At a maximizing mark every fixed-normal buffered cap has mass at least Q. Hence each adjusted threshold is at most the right Q-quantile. The weighted sum of the threshold differences is exactly the corrected base displacement plus ε times the nonnegative full-support deficit. This follows from Σρ_j=1 and Σρ_j u_j=εg. If the displacement is zero, positivity of all ρ_j forces every difference to vanish, so the same physical regular cap binds at both marks.

Positive total coarea gives a fiber with positive section area. In that fiber a fixed interior point off the section plane creates, by convexity, homothetic parallel sections of uniformly positive area on one side arbitrarily near the threshold. Its slab contribution gives a strictly negative symmetric threshold difference quotient bounded away from zero. The C^1 hypothesis implies ∂_c m<0.

The implicit function theorem gives a locally differentiable mass-Q threshold. Strict decrease on a neighborhood and global monotonicity exclude any larger right Q-quantile. Holding normalized u fixed is allowed because its norm does not depend on a. At each fixed maximizing mark the difference between its affine-in-a threshold and that quantile is at most zero for all a and equals zero at the same a. Their gradients would give both p and r in the affine base chart. This forces p=r, and strictness on I\{p} exposes exactly {p} on conv(I).

For polytopes, a supporting section of positive (d−1)-measure is a full facet section and corresponds to one of finitely many closed plane-coincidence conditions on the full parameters. Excluding all such conditions in other fibers and preserving the proper own trace is open. The accepted directional formula therefore applies throughout a neighborhood.

Identify nearby section planes by isometries tending to the identity. At a proper section the sections converge in Hausdorff distance, since points in the relative interior of that section are interior to the full-dimensional fiber. At a null supporting section, compactness confines nearby sections to arbitrarily small neighborhoods of the limiting zero-measure section. Areas and first moments converge in both cases. The full cap mass is locally Lipschitz by the common slab bound and the continuous normal stays bounded away from zero. For directions varying along a sequence, compare to a convergent fixed direction using the same Lipschitz constant, which upgrades the linear directional derivative to a full derivative. The continuous coefficients give C^1 regularity.

In d=1 a supporting singleton has positive H_0 measure and is correctly excluded from the null-section case. As an exact check, unit intervals over 0 and 1 with a=1/2,u=1,c=1/2 have a proper own trace and a supporting point in the second fiber. Their threshold derivatives are −1 on the left and −2 on the right. Original c3bb7df3660a88b5 §6, Proposition 6 and (9), has the same strict-resultant and polytopal claims.
